catalog_quote: 3.1.2 Word-internal metrical structure. Paleni does not have a discernible stress system. However, there are hints of a subtle prosodic organization into CvCv and Cvv units starting at the left edge of stems. The effect is that CvCv and Cvv are unbroken units, while CvvCv and CvCvCv have internal breaks. Oddly, the evidence for this seems to point in opposite directions, with the Cv_v position favoring lenition in one context and fortition (gemination) in another. Cv_v is favorable to voiced stops varying with voiceless unaspirated stops, while Cvv_v and CvCv_v are favorable to unvoiced aspirated stops. This appears to be systematic for velar stops, and a tendency for other obstruents (§3.2.1.1.1). In this case, Cv_v is a weakening position for consonants. In verbs, the (n)n reflecting hardening of stem-final nasal coda N before a vowel is heard as geminated nn after monosyllabic Cvⁿ stems, but as simple n after longer stems (including Cvvⁿ and CvCvⁿ) (§3.4.1.7). ... In this case, Cv_v is a strengthening position for consonants.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File (426 pp., the PDF's metadata gives the author Jeffrey Heath, created 2026-08-12; Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21904854). extracted text gives printed page number 13 and the heading '3.1.2 Word-internal metrical structure' followed by the quoted passage word for word: 'Paleni does not have a discernible stress system. However, there are hints of a subtle prosodic organization into CvCv and Cvv units starting at the left edge of stems. new_statements.rule_in_words: Paleni is a three-level tone language (H, M, L) with no discernible word-stress system; the only prosodic word-internal structure the author detects is a weak left-edge grouping of stems into CvCv/Cvv units, diagnosed by consonant lenition vs. gemination sites, not by stress.
new_statements.exceptions: None as to stress; author notes only 'hints' of left-edge metrical grouping (Cv_v position conditions voicing/lenition of velar stops and nn-gemination in monosyllabic Cvⁿ verb stems). Intonational effects are phrase-final (sec. 2.1.5, 3.7).
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about word-internal (stem/word) prosody; tone is lexical and grammatical (tonal ablaut); intonation treated separately at prosodic-phrase ends.
new_statements.identity_note: Heath's 'Paleni' = Glottolog pale1262 Palen (ISO pnl), the language of the single village Faniagara (Léraba province, Burkina Faso); Heath cites Glottolog 5.2 'Palen' and Kleinewillinghöfer's spelling 'Palɛn' explicitly (sec. 1.2, 1.2.1), autonym pálɛ̀-nì. Data from speakers Traoré Adama and son Boukari of Faniagara plus 2024/2026 village recordings. Not to be confused with Samue/Wara (wara1292, Niansogoni etc.), for which Ouattara 2015 separately reports 'no overt stress'.

sources.note: Sec. 3.1.2 'Word-internal metrical structure', printed p.13 (p.29): 'Paleni does not have a discernible stress system'; only hints of subtle prosodic grouping into CvCv/Cvv units from the left edge of stems (lenition vs gemination sites). Language has three tone levels H/M/L (sec. 2.1.2 p.5; ch. 3.6); intonation phrase-final (2.1.5, 3.7).
